question.text: Create a review table for three item types from lessons 8-15. For each one, write the item type, the main skill tested, one problem you have had, and one strategy or solution to try.

answer.text: A strong answer names specific item types, links each one to a relevant skill, identifies a real problem, and gives a practical next step. Example: Re-tell lecture: listening and speaking; problem: weak recall; solution: practise note-taking and recall skills.

question.text: After comparing two versions of an assessment form, what three things should you record about your progress?

answer.text: Record what has improved, what remains problematic, and what solution or strategy you will try next with a partner or group.

question.text: Choose one area from the homework overview that could be a useful focus for extra practice. Explain why that focus fits the item type.

answer.text: A suitable answer connects an item type to its focus area. Example: for Re-tell lecture, note-taking, listening, and recall are useful because the overview notes those as possible focus areas for that item type.

question.text: What should a group do when it still has unresolved questions after discussing practice problems?

answer.text: The group should bring remaining problems to the whole class, discuss them, and use the Official Guide or information from lesson plans 8-15 when quick clarification is possible.

review_checklist.text: I can name the item types covered in lessons 8-15 and describe the skills each one requires.
I can identify which item types and skills I feel confident about and which ones need more practice.
I can explain at least one problem I had with a practice item and one solution I will try.
I have compared my current self-assessment with an earlier one and noted my progress.
I can choose extra practice based on my own problem areas rather than reviewing randomly.
I have a plan for continuing to improve my speaking, writing, reading, and listening skills.
